label: dense: active almost everywhere except the <DEL> step; strongest at first 3 original tokens and in copy phase
explanation: Dense feature active on 71% of all steps and in every sequence. Its only clear structure is positional: always on at t=0 (rate 1.0), 0.92 at t=1, 0.77 at t=2, then falling through the middle and end of the original phase (rate 0.25-0.5 at orig_idx>=4); mostly off at the <DEL> step (rate 0.16); on for about 88% of copy-phase steps at every recall_idx. Token identity, L, digits, next_out, and first_tok barely change the rate (lift 0.9-1.2x). The predicate (phase==2)|(t<3) gets precision ~0.89 and F1 ~0.85, and phase!=1 gets F1 ~0.86, but both scores mostly reflect the high base rate, not a specific concept. The largest activations come from particular early-prefix contents (e.g. f f x at t=2), which no simple variable captures. No monosemantic description was found.
